input.rationale: Source-only refinement with the remaining allocation, no execution. The wedge finding's repair set was executed on both routes, but one operational boundary stayed implicit: how soon the snapshot route can be reached in a default deployment. Reading the compaction and replication code settles it, so it is recorded as a behaviour with its anchors rather than left as prose in a limitation.

knowledge.statement: The snapshot route that repairs a wedged follower is reached only when the leader can no longer read the entry the follower needs: setPreviousLog/setNewLogs call the leader's log store, and an error there is what produces ErrLogNotFound and the SEND_SNAP path. Compaction keeps the trailing window, so a snapshot at index S does not remove entries below min(S, lastLogIdx - TrailingLogs); with the default TrailingLogs of 10240 and the default snapshot threshold of 8192, the leader's log must therefore advance roughly ten thousand entries beyond the snapshot before the entries a wedged follower asks for are gone. A wedged follower whose next index is pinned near the beginning is consequently not repaired by the snapshot route soon after the wedge in a default configuration, and the restart path or an explicit compaction configuration (as used in the executed experiment) is what makes the repair available.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state with default Config values (TrailingLogs 10240, SnapshotThreshold 8192, SnapshotInterval 120s); a follower whose replication is pinned at an early index, so the leader would have to read entries below its first stored index to serve it.

knowledge.statement: For an explicit leadership transfer (LeadershipTransferToServer) the leader accepts the caller-supplied target if and only if a followerReplication entry exists for that ServerID in leaderState.replState; the only rejection is a target equal to the local ID ('cannot transfer leadership to itself'). No suffrage test is applied at the API, at initiateLeadershipTransfer, or at the leaderLoop hand-off to leadershipTransfer.
knowledge.conditions: protocolVersion >= 3, node is in Leader state and processing the leadershipTransferCh case on the main thread; the caller supplies an ID present in configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: startStopReplication starts a followerReplication goroutine for every server in configurations.latest whose ID differs from the local ID, with no suffrage filter, so leaderState.replState (the map consulted by the explicit transfer path and by pickServer) also contains Nonvoter members. pickServer, by contrast, skips 'server.Suffrage != Voter', so the targetless transfer path cannot select a non-voter.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state, after appendConfigurationEntry/setLatestConfiguration followed by startStopReplication.

knowledge.statement: On receiving a TimeoutNowRequest a node clears its known leader, sets its state to Candidate and sets candidateFromLeadershipTransfer to true, then acknowledges. The handler performs no term comparison (TimeoutNowRequest carries no term), no state check, no suffrage check on the receiver, and no check that the sender is the current leader or a configuration member; runCandidate then skips pre-vote for such a candidate and calls electSelf directly.
knowledge.conditions: The RPC passes checkRPCHeader (protocol version range) and is dispatched from processRPC on the main thread.

knowledge.statement: In requestVote, when a RequestVote arrives with req.Term > currentTerm the receiver first steps down (setState(Follower)) and adopts the higher term, and only afterwards rejects the request because the candidate is not a Voter ('rejecting vote request since node is not a voter'), returning Granted false. Because the step-down precedes the rejection, a term-advancing vote request from an unelectable candidate still removes the receiver from leadership.
knowledge.conditions: Receiver is a Voter or Leader with a non-empty configurations.latest.Servers, and the candidate passes the inConfiguration check.

knowledge.statement: In appendEntries, when a received entry conflicts with one the node already stores, the node deletes the range [entry.Index, lastLogIdx] via logs.DeleteRange, then stores the replacement entries via logs.StoreLogs. If StoreLogs returns an error the handler logs 'failed to append to logs' and returns before any setLastLog call: the in-memory lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm keep the values they had before the deletion (the code marks this with a TODO), and no other branch in the receive path restores them. The response for that request is left with Success false.
knowledge.conditions: Follower/Candidate state; a.Term not older than the node's current term; at least one received entry whose index is at or below the node's last log index and whose term differs from the stored entry; and an error return from logs.StoreLogs for that call.

knowledge.statement: The in-memory last-log certificate is read through raftState.getLastEntry (and getLastIndex, which takes the maximum of lastLogIndex and lastSnapshotIndex, so a snapshot does not mask a stale log index). Its consumers are: electSelf and preElectSelf, which put it in RequestVoteRequest/RequestPreVoteRequest as LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm; requestVote/requestPreVote, which use it to decide whether to grant a vote; appendEntries, which compares it against PrevLogEntry to validate a leader's previous entry; and Raft.LastIndex, the public accessor. None of these consult the LogStore.
knowledge.conditions: Any node, whenever it campaigns or answers a vote request or validates an AppendEntries previous entry.

knowledge.statement: In the appendEntries entry loop the comparison 'entry.Index > lastLogIdx' uses lastLogIdx read from the in-memory certificate (getLastLog), not from the log store. For an entry at or below that cached index the handler calls logs.GetLog(entry.Index) and returns immediately if it errors, so once the conflicting suffix has been deleted from the store, any re-sent entry covering those indices makes the handler return before StoreLogs is reached. The certificate is never re-derived from the store inside this handler.
knowledge.conditions: Follower or Candidate state with at least one entry in the request whose index is at or below the cached last log index while that index is absent from the store (the state produced by a failed StoreLogs immediately after a conflicting-suffix deletion).

knowledge.statement: On an unsuccessful AppendEntries response the leader sets the peer's nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, resp.LastLog+1), 1). When the follower's response carries a LastLog at or above the leader's index, the value settles at 1 (or at the floor) and the leader re-sends the same request, so a follower that rejects for a self-inflicted reason is re-driven with an identical request rather than a snapshot; ErrLogNotFound leading to SEND_SNAP is only produced from the leader's own log store, not from the follower's response.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; the follower responds Success=false with a LastLog hint at or above the leader's last index.

knowledge.statement: A single allowed error return from LogStore.StoreLogs in the call that follows a conflicting-suffix deletion leaves the follower unable to converge: its durable log keeps the truncated state (its last index falls to the last surviving index before the conflict), its cached last-log certificate keeps describing the deleted suffix, its commit and applied indexes stop advancing, and no further StoreLogs call is even attempted, so removing the error afterwards does not restore progress.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport, one follower holding an isolated uncommitted tail appended at an earlier term, a higher-term leader with committed replacement entries at the same indices, and exactly one allowed StoreLogs error on the replacement write; the fault may be removed afterwards without changing the outcome. In the observed run the same history with a healthy store converged inside the window (store 1..5, certificate (5,3), commit and applied 5) while the faulted node stayed at store last 2, certificate (4,2) and commit and applied 2 for 2.7 s.

knowledge.statement: When the wedged replica from the conflict-truncation store-error state is one of three voters, the cluster cannot commit any new entry after a single further voter loss: the leader accepts the entry into its own log (store and certificate advance to the new index) but its commit index stays at the value it had before and the client's apply future never completes, whereas the control run of the identical history without the store error commits the same entry as soon as the peer-loss phase begins. The wedged replica's store last index and StoreLogs attempt counter are unchanged across the phase, so its match index cannot advance and the quorum of match indexes can no longer include the new entry.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport; one voter left in the conflict-truncation store-error state (store truncated, cached certificate stale, no further store writes); one further voter removed; one client entry applied on the remaining leader. Observed for 1500 ms with 25 ms sampling, with the matching control run in the same execution.

knowledge.statement: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry and then, without waiting for it to commit, sets configurations.latest to the new configuration and calls leaderState.commitment.setConfiguration, which rebuilds the match-index map so that every voter of the new configuration is counted, with servers that have never answered starting at 0. The quorum decisions for commitment therefore use the new configuration from that moment, while configurations.committed still describes the old one.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; any successful configuration change request (AddVoter, AddNonvoter, DemoteVoter, RemoveServer) whose entry has been appended but not yet committed.

knowledge.statement: Both the leader lease check and the election path read configurations.latest, not the committed configuration: checkLeaderLease counts contacted voters of the latest configuration and demotes the leader when that count is below the latest configuration's quorum size, and quorumSize (used by candidates to decide when they have won) is computed from the same latest configuration. An uncommitted configuration whose quorum requires a server that never answers therefore both blocks commitment and removes the surviving servers' ability to keep or regain leadership.
knowledge.conditions: A node whose configurations.latest includes a voter added by a configuration entry that has not committed, while that voter is unreachable.

knowledge.statement: The timeout accepted by the configuration-change APIs bounds only the attempt to hand the request to the main loop: requestConfigChange returns errorFuture{ErrEnqueueTimeout} if the timer fires before the request is queued, otherwise it returns the future whose Error blocks until the configuration entry commits. A caller cannot use that timeout to learn that the configuration change is stuck.
knowledge.conditions: Any AddVoter/AddNonvoter/DemoteVoter/RemoveServer call with a non-zero timeout.

knowledge.statement: On a single-voter cluster, AddVoter for a server that is not running yet commits the configuration change (the leader's own match is recorded against the previous configuration's quorum) and the future completes successfully, after which the only node loses leadership within the lease timeout and remains a Candidate that cannot be re-elected under the configuration it just committed, so client writes are refused with ErrNotLeader until the named server appears; pre-vote keeps its term unchanged throughout, and starting the named server restores leadership.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3, a configuration with exactly one voter grown by one voter (so the new configuration's quorum cannot be met by the surviving server), the named server not running, no faults, in-memory transport. Observed with 25 ms sampling for 1500 ms after the call, with the same call on an equivalent cluster whose named server was already running as the control.

knowledge.statement: A wedged replica (conflict-truncation store-error state) does not converge while running, even after the store error is removed, but a restart over the same durable state does converge: after restarting the same stores with a fresh transport at the same address, the certificate, the store's last index and the commit index return to the leader's values and the leader's re-sent entries are stored (certificate (5,3) versus the wedged (4,2), commit 0 to 5).
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster, in-memory transport, the store wrapper's error no longer injected; restart modelled as NewRaft over the same log store, stable store and snapshot store with a new transport at the same address and the peers rewired (Shutdown closes the transport it was built with). Observed for four seconds after the restart with 200 ms sampling.

knowledge.statement: commitment keeps one match index per voter of the current configuration and takes the quorum match index as the middle of the sorted values, so a voter whose stored log can never advance holds its slot at the stuck index for as long as the configuration stands. The wedged replica therefore consumes exactly one unit of the configuration's failure margin: the remaining voters must be able to form a quorum on their own, which in a three-voter configuration is impossible once one other voter is gone and in a five-voter configuration only becomes impossible when two other voters are gone.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; a voter whose durable log is stuck below the leader's committed prefix while it remains a member of configurations.latest; commitment.setConfiguration has been applied for that configuration.

history.statement: commitment keeps one match index per voter of the current configuration and takes the quorum match index as the middle of the sorted values, so a voter whose stored log can never advance holds its slot at the stuck index for as long as the configuration stands. The wedged replica therefore consumes exactly one unit of the configuration's failure margin: the remaining voters must be able to form a quorum on their own, which in a three-voter configuration is impossible once one other voter is gone and in a five-voter configuration only becomes impossible when two other voters are gone.
history.conditions: Leader state; a voter whose durable log is stuck below the leader's committed prefix while it remains a member of configurations.latest; commitment.setConfiguration has been applied for that configuration.

knowledge.statement: A wedged replica (conflict-truncation store-error state) is also repaired by the library's own snapshot machinery: when the leader's log has been compacted so it can no longer serve the entries the follower needs, the leader sends an InstallSnapshot, after which the follower's certificate, store bounds, commit and applied indexes catch up to the snapshot and the new entry (certificate (4,2) to (6,3), store 1..2 to 6..6, commit 2 to 6), and replication resumes from the snapshot boundary.
knowledge.conditions: Three-voter cluster over an in-memory transport, one follower in the conflict-truncation store-error state with the fault no longer injected, leader compaction configured (snapshot threshold 1, trailing logs 0, snapshot interval one hour) and a snapshot taken through the public Snapshot API; observed for four seconds after a new client entry with 200 ms sampling.

knowledge.statement: After the documented growth step has made a single-voter cluster leaderless because the newly named server is absent, the same API cannot undo it: RemoveServer and AddNonvoter for that server both return ErrNotLeader, a client write is refused with the same error, and the node remains a Candidate with an unchanged term and a pinned commit index for the whole observed window; the only observed repair is starting the named server, after which the original node wins an election and progress resumes.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3, one-voter configuration grown by one voter with the new server not running, no faults, in-memory transport; 1500 ms of sampling after the growth call plus two bounded (1200 ms) repair attempts and a further three seconds of sampling. The control with the named server running beforehand accepts both repair calls and keeps serving.

knowledge.statement: On a single-voter cluster, naming a server that is not running yet through AddNonvoter keeps the cluster serving: the leader stays Leader with an unchanged term, the configuration entry commits, and client writes succeed; the same staging through AddVoter leaves the cluster leaderless and refusing writes. The difference is the suffrage the named server receives, since a non-voter is excluded from commitment and from the lease quorum while a voter is counted immediately.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3, one-voter configuration grown by one member that is not running (unwired transport, no raft instance), in-memory transport, no faults; 1500 ms of 25 ms sampling plus a bounded client write, with the AddVoter and AddNonvoter forms run as separate cases in the same execution.

knowledge.statement: AddVoter's documentation still describes the deprecated staged behaviour ('will add the given server to the cluster as a staging server ... The leader will promote the staging server to a voter once that server is ready'), and BootstrapCluster's documentation recommends growing a cluster exactly that way (bootstrap one voter, then AddVoter the next server). The code does neither: appendConfigurationEntry installs the named server as a voter in configurations.latest and in the commitment map immediately, so in the documented growth step from one voter the surviving node's lease quorum and election quorum already require the new server. The caller-visible result is a successful AddVoter future, so the API reports success for a step that has just made the cluster unavailable until that server runs.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3, single-voter configuration grown by one voter whose server is not running; witnessed by the cited execution, in which the configuration entry committed, the AddVoter future returned nil, the node left leadership and stayed a Candidate, and the cluster recovered only once the named server was started.

knowledge.statement: LeadershipTransferToServer's documentation offers to transfer leadership to 'a specific server in the cluster' and promises that a transfer which cannot complete 'will fail gracefully', while the code path accepts any server for which replication state exists, including a Nonvoter, and the protocol refuses to elect a non-voter candidate. Naming a non-voter therefore deposes the incumbent leader without transferring anything, and the future can still report success, so neither the documented eligibility restriction nor the documented graceful failure is what the caller receives.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3, three voters plus a caught-up Nonvoter added through AddNonvoter; witnessed by the cited execution, in which the transfer future returned nil while the named target never became Leader and the incumbent stepped down.

// Reject if their term is older
	lastIdx, lastTerm := r.getLastEntry()
	if lastTerm > req.LastLogTerm {
		r.logger.Warn("rejecting vote request since our last term is greater",
			"candidate", candidate,
			"last-term", lastTerm,
			"last-candidate-term", req.LastLogTerm)
		return
	}

	if lastTerm == req.LastLogTerm && lastIdx > req.LastLogIndex {
		r.logger.Warn("rejecting vote request since our last index is greater",
			"candidate", candidate,
			"last-index", lastIdx,
			"last-candidate-index", req.LastLogIndex)
		return

knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 3, three voters plus a caught-up Nonvoter added through AddNonvoter; witnessed by the cited execution, in which the transfer future returned nil while the named target never became Leader and the incumbent stepped down.

knowledge.statement: The snapshot route that repairs a wedged follower is reached only when the leader can no longer read the entry the follower needs: setPreviousLog/setNewLogs call the leader's log store, and an error there is what produces ErrLogNotFound and the SEND_SNAP path. Compaction keeps the trailing window, so a snapshot at index S does not remove entries below min(S, lastLogIdx - TrailingLogs); with the default TrailingLogs of 10240 and the default snapshot threshold of 8192, the leader's log must therefore advance roughly ten thousand entries beyond the snapshot before the entries a wedged follower asks for are gone. A wedged follower whose next index is pinned near the beginning is consequently not repaired by the snapshot route soon after the wedge in a default configuration, and the restart path or an explicit compaction configuration (as used in the executed experiment) is what makes the repair available.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state with default Config values (TrailingLogs 10240, SnapshotThreshold 8192, SnapshotInterval 120s); a follower whose replication is pinned at an early index, so the leader would have to read entries below its first stored index to serve it.

			"last-candidate-index", req.LastLogIndex)
